editorial:
Imagine finding out your dad is alive, but the only way to get close to him is by pretending to be a guy. That is exactly the wild ride you get with this French comedy. You follow Frédérique, a woman who inherits a farm and decides to track down her mystery father in Paris. Things get crazy when she hangs out with her best friend Marc and ends up dressing up as 'Frédéric,' an effeminate young man, just to get into a gay bar. The movie has a light, bubbly energy that makes you root for her, even as she gets tangled in a giant web of lies while trying to bond with her art curator father.

You will love how the lead actress handles the double role; the physical comedy of her trying to act like a boy is genuinely funny. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the awkward family dynamics keep you interested. It is a sweet story about identity and family, though it is more of a quirky romp than a deep drama. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your collection for a cozy movie night. It is a great pick if you enjoy stories about mistaken identity.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the lie becomes too big to handle. Frédérique eventually reveals her true identity to Pierre, her father. Instead of being angry, Pierre accepts her, and they finally build a real father-daughter relationship based on honesty. She stops pretending to be a boy and finds a balance between her old life and her new family. It ends on a happy, warm note where everyone accepts each other for who they really are.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy comedies and stories about family secrets.
